elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience may take effect on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least one calendar month's prior written notice and permits termination only at the end of a calendar month. A calendar month is not necessarily 30 days, and the month-end restriction can delay effectiveness beyond 30 days.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: IBM must refund any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective termination date, which substantively provides the required unused-period pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language grants a termination-for-convenience right only to Customer and grants IBM no such right, including during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice requirement is only at least one calendar month. The month-end effectiveness restriction does not establish a notice period consistently between 60 and 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The redline caps applicable early termination charges, in the aggregate, at three months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience may take effect only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The supplied language grants IBM no termination-for-convenience right at all, which is more protective than permitting such termination only at term end; the condition for this restriction is therefore absent.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The supplied language grants IBM no termination-for-convenience right, so the conditional Vendor notice requirement is not triggered.

result.reason: The redline clearly adds the fallback-compliant three-month early-termination-charge cap and a substantively pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges. However, it retains the one-calendar-month notice requirement and month-end effectiveness restriction, satisfying neither the preferred 30-day mechanic nor the fallback 60–90-day notice range. Because no complete level is achieved and the redline combines additions drawn from different levels without correcting the dispositive notice provision, it is not minimal. The additions do not contradict or disturb unrelated commercial terms.
